Description: Family estate from Fèrebrianges in the Vallée du Petit Morin. A. Bergère owns 45 hectares of vineyards and works with a strong terroir- and parcel-focused approach, with a clear emphasis on Chardonnay and low dosage. In addition to its home base, the estate also owns parcels in the Côte des Blancs and the Sézannais.
History: The family has been growing grapes in Fèrebrianges since 1848. Albert Bergère began producing Champagne himself in 1949 and founded Maison A. Bergère. André Bergère took over the estate in 1986 and expanded its vineyard holdings. Annaëlle joined in 2009 and manages the activities in Épernay; oenologist Adrien Bergère took over winemaking in 2014 and introduced an even stronger parcel-by-parcel approach.
Terroir: 45 ha of estate-owned vineyards, around 35 ha of which are in the Vallée du Petit Morin around Fèrebrianges, Étoges and Congy. There are 139 parcels in total. The estate also owns Chardonnay terroirs in the Côte des Blancs and Sézannais, including Avize, Oger, Le Mesnil-sur-Oger, Cramant and Chouilly. The soils are predominantly chalky and clay-limestone.
Wine Style: Terroir-driven and precise, with separate vinification of the 139 parcels. Fermentation may be spontaneous or use yeasts selected from the estate’s own vineyards; malolactic fermentation is used. Ageing takes place in stainless steel, oak barrels and foudres, with long lees ageing and blending without fining or filtration. Many cuvées have a low dosage or are Brut Nature.
Grapes: Vineyard plantings: approximately 70% Chardonnay, 20% Pinot Noir and 10% Meunier. The house also makes a rare 100% Petit Meslier cuvée.
Visitor Information: Tasting room and boutique at 38–40 Avenue de Champagne in Épernay, open year-round. Estate and cellar visits in Fèrebrianges are available by reservation; the extended tour departs from Épernay and includes vineyards, the domaine, cellars and a tasting. Chambres d’hôtes and suites are also available in Épernay.
Prestige Cuvée: No formally designated prestige cuvée; the top and iconic wines include Petit Meslier, Blanc de Blancs Grand Cru Extra-Brut and the single-parcel cuvées Les Peignottes and Les Clos.
Maison Director: André Bergère (estate management, with Brigitte); Annaëlle Bergère manages the activities in Épernay
Cellars: Production and ageing cellars at the estate in Fèrebrianges; also a tasting cellar/caveau beneath Avenue de Champagne in Épernay.
Cellar Location: Domaine: 57 Grande Rue, 51270 Fèrebrianges. Caveau/tasting room: 38-40 Avenue de Champagne, 51200 Épernay.

Description: Historic Champagne Maison in Reims, founded in 1757 and presented by the house as the fifth-oldest Champagne Maison. Abelé 1757 works in small volumes with an artisanal, premium style centred on Chardonnay, long ageing and precision.
History: Founded in 1757 by Théodore VanderVeken. In 1816, according to the house history, Antoine de Muller, grandfather of Henri Abelé and cellar master at Veuve Clicquot, developed an early riddling table. Henri Abelé took over the family business in 1876 and gave the house his name; he was also among the early users of ice disgorgement. The Maison has a strong connection with the Smiling Angel of Reims Cathedral. In 2019 Abelé was acquired by the predecessor of TEVC; since 2021 the house has used the name Abelé 1757.
Terroir: Abelé does not own one large contiguous estate, but selects grapes through a small circle of long-standing partner growers. Important origins include the Côte des Blancs, Montagne de Reims, Sézannais, Vitryat and Les Riceys. Chardonnay forms the core of the house style; Pinot Noir from areas including Les Riceys plays an important role in the rosés.
Wine Style: Refined, fresh and precise, with Chardonnay as the dominant signature. The Maison works with small production volumes, carefully selected terroirs and reserve wines. Non-vintage cuvées generally age for around 3–4 years; the prestige cuvées Le Sourire de Reims for at least 10 years. The style combines fine mousse, minerality, ripeness and a long finish, with relatively restrained dosages.
Grapes: Chardonnay (dominant), Pinot Noir and Meunier. Le Sourire de Reims Rosé uses 100% Pinot Noir from Les Riceys.
Visitor Information: Maison at 50 Rue de Sillery in Reims. The historic cellars are not normally open to the general public on a regular basis, but are occasionally opened for special events and exclusive visits. Current opportunities are arranged through the Maison and selected tourism events in Reims.
Prestige Cuvée: Le Sourire de Reims: Brut Millésimé 2013 (60% Chardonnay, 40% Pinot Noir) and Rosé 2008 (100% Pinot Noir from Les Riceys, rosé de saignée). Both age for at least 10 years.
Cellars: Approximately 2 km of historic chalk cellars/crayères, divided into around 30 galleries, about 20–25 metres underground. The constant cool temperature, darkness and humidity are used for long bottle ageing.
Cellar Location: 50 Rue de Sillery, 51100 Reims, at the foot of the Butte Saint-Nicaise.
